name: # Dataset classification for the pathological-data doctrine (README: "Role of pathological data").
# name = dataset as spelled in the configs dataset column, or config:<name> for inline-prep
# configs and per-config overrides (an override wins over the dataset lookup - used where a
# prep/ifcond materially changes the effective class of the data the run actually sees).
# coverage_check.py --data-classes consumes this and fails on any drift (unclassified config / stale row).
dta_binary
rationale: Rich staggered panel: 80 units (25 treated 2005, 25 treated 2008, 30 never-treated), 12 periods, unit FEs, subgroups, weights, count outcome, heterogeneous cohort effects. Trustworthy results by design; the main core battery workhorse (34 configs).

name: dta_cont
rationale: Repo continuous-treatment example, seeded: 10 units (5 treated at t=5, 5 never), 10 periods, 10 draws per cell (1000 obs), near-noiseless outcome with known dose effect. The canonical feature-evidence dataset for continuous treatment (11 core configs).

name: dta_path_imbalanced
rationale: Imbalanced panel (unit spans 2-12 periods) with staggered cohorts and never-treated controls — heavy attrition (27 of 30 units exit early; no late entry and no internal holes; at t=12 one never-treated unit is the whole control pool - datasets audit 2026-09-12); main results still usable. Carries config-gated traps: extraFE singleton inducer (fires only under fe(extraFE)) and sg=.a sentinel on one unit.

name: dta_path_nocontrols
rationale: Every one of 20 units treated at the same time ttre=4 — no controls of any kind, so no counterfactual exists. Generator comment says it is for error-path testing and must fail informatively.

name: dta_path_nonever
rationale: Staggered onsets (4/7/9) with zero never-treated units — a design wooldid intentionally rejects (r459). Exists to verify the rejection stays informative, not to be run to results.

name: dta_path_nopost
rationale: One cohort's onset (ttre=9) falls after the sample ends (T=8) — an unusual-but-holdable coding: those units are valid control-like observations, and wooldid documents this handling (oostreatedcontrols). The ttre=5 cohort and never-treated units yield usable results.

name: dta_path_nopre
rationale: One cohort (8 of 24 units) treated at the first sample period: no pre-period exists, so no baseline is constructible and no trustworthy number can exist for that cohort — correct behavior is an observable drop or error. Also a sentinel sg=.a unit.

name: dta_path_onepercell
rationale: Exactly one unit per treatment-cohort cell (4 single-unit cohorts plus 2 never-treated units, 6 units total). Single-observation cells are degenerate by construction: within-cohort variation and cluster inference are inestimable.

name: dta_path_relyrgap
rationale: Well-formed staggered panel (10+10 treated, 10 never, 10 periods) with two surgically removed relative-year cells, including cohort A's default reference period (relyr -1). Calendar gaps are stress by scheme; alternate references exist, and three core configs use it as gap-handling feature evidence.

name: dta_path_sep
rationale: Engineered Poisson separation: one never-treated unit with all-zero counts (unit-level separation) and one treated cohort-period cell forced to zero. Perfect separation is pathological by scheme; the doctored ycount is the dataset's reason for existing, and its only config runs the poisson separation trigger.

name: dta_simple1
rationale: Repo simple example verbatim, seeded: 10 units, cohorts at t=3 and t=7 plus 4 never-treated, 10 periods, huge effect-to-noise ratio (effect 3 or 7 vs sd 0.11). Clean, trustworthy, non-degenerate.

name: dta_tiny
rationale: Minimal but structurally complete: 8 units (3 treated at t=4, 5 never-treated), 6 periods, pre and post both present. Point estimates usable; smallness is functional (scr_permexact_t exists because tiny N makes permutation enumeration exact). One subgroup has a single treated unit.

name: dta_s_admin
rationale: Realistic administrative-style county panel: ~2,000 FIPS units x 2005-2019, unequal staggered cohorts with a ~25% never pool, lognormal population weights, mild realistic imbalance (~4% late entry/early exit) and ~2% regular-missing y. All 11 adm configs read it for realistic feature coverage; result differences here are feature-quality signal.

name: dta_s_biennial
rationale: Biennial survey grid 1997-2019 (spacing 2) with the 2009 wave missing for every unit (datasets audit P2, 2026-09-13): 120 units, onsets 2003/2011 (30 each) + 60 never, sg 40/80, gamma aw weight w, a zero-free count ycount (unit-level i plus a zero singleton treated cell is a separation refusal on HEAD); N 1320 = 120 x 11 waves. Relative year -1 exists for no cohort and cohort 2011's relative year -2 is the hole. Trustworthy answers where the horizon exists (att-only unbiased across seeds on the audit probe); esfixedbaseperiod esrelativeto(-2) legitimately drops cohort 2011, odd horizons are empty, anticipation(1) lands off-grid - an unusual-but-holdable calendar, hence stress.

name: dta_s_bigcodes
rationale: Clean balanced 40x12 panel whose only awkwardness is extreme-but-realistic codings: consecutive unit IDs at 3e7 (float spacing 2, so float-casting provably pools units) and a YYYYMMDD month-start time grid. Small-recode twin columns (i_small/t_small/ttre_small) make the correct answer well-defined; y is built from the small codes so both codings target identical estimands.

name: dta_s_covars
rationale: Rich well-behaved 150x12 base panel (y built from complete controls plus effects and noise) carrying deliberately awkward pockets: injected missing x1/x2 (~3% of rows), three single-row singleton fecat levels, and the defective icbad probe column (1e6-level unit-constant-plus-t control). Column-dependent: cov_ic/cov_ccc/cov_cwm run clean columns (feature signal); cov_icbad/cov_icbad2 run the engineered probe; dominant use is coverage with awkward structure, so stress.

name: dta_s_deeppre
rationale: Balanced 60-unit x 14-period panel, two 20-unit cohorts (onset 8/10) plus 20 never-treated, genuine treatment effect and Gaussian noise. The A14 trigger lives in the config options (adversarial esf, esrelativeto(-3), subgroups), not in the data; the dataset supports trustworthy non-degenerate results.

name: dta_s_extmiss
rationale: Faithful clone of the well-behaved dta_binary panel with extended missings (.a) injected into y/t/w on ~2-2.5% of rows each — ordinary Stata coding practice, deliberately awkward. A trustworthy answer exists by construction (the cleaned-reference twin: drop the extended-missing rows), which is exactly what the pathological class excludes; the case tests missing-value robustness on otherwise sound data.

name: dta_s_imdegen
rationale: Engineered IM-inference degeneracy: NOISELESS outcomes that are exact functions of cohort group, t, and horizon, with clusters built orthogonal to cohort, so every per-cluster estimate is numerically identical and IM variance is degenerate by construction. Both columns are degenerate — y fully (all cells flagged), ypart partially (structural-zero pre cells, A17 sentinel path); ypart is NOT a clean twin. Only question: missing-SE-plus-Caution vs zero-diagonal e(V).

name: dta_s_mintsent
rationale: Both suite configs run deliberately defective onset codings: ttre records onset only from the onset period onward (within-unit varying/missing — invalid design, drawing the new r459 refusal) and ttre_sent plants a sentinel 0 in unit 1's pre-onset rows (sentinel coding is on the scheme's explicit pathological list; v1.3 silently biased). The clean twin ttre_good exists but no suite config uses it, so the dominant intended use is bad-input handling.

name: dta_s_singleton
rationale: Imbalanced 40-unit panel with engineered singleton pockets — 4 never-treated units observed exactly once, three single-row fevar levels (two on treated post rows), 14 scattered mod() row drops — but the generator deliberately preserves estimability: every treated unit keeps >=2 pre rows and the comment says att_it is well-defined. Results remain usable; the trigger is e(sample)-accounting correctness under reghdfe singleton drops.

name: dta_s_stateyear
rationale: Realistic county-in-state policy panel (datasets audit P1, 2026-09-13): 12 states of 5-12 counties (106 units) x 1995-2014, six STATE-level onset cohorts (1999/2002/2005/2008/2011/2013 with 17/21/6/19/5/10 counties, incl. one-state cohorts of 5-6 counties and a 2-post-period cohort) plus 3 never states (28 counties); AR(1) .6 county errors with county-level heteroskedasticity and a state-by-year shock (y; y_nosh drops the shock for i=st runs; y_dose is the no-shock continuous-dose outcome), heterogeneous dynamic effects, a 20/80 county subgroup sg, a 3-level state subgroup region (one never-treated state in each), lognormal pop (aw/pw), a count outcome ycount (~20% zeros), county-level dose_it varying within every state-year cell; 8 late-entry / 4 early-exit counties, interior holes on 45 counties, 33 missing y (1.6%); N 2050. Trustworthy answers by design: the realistic bed for cluster-above-i inference (bootstrap/permute/impvalues at 12 states) and, with i=st cluster(unit) on y_nosh/y_dose, the only suite data where jointtests/adversarial/timetrends/contreat post an identified analytic variance on stochastic data. Its known degeneracies are config-level, not data-level: config:real_sg (county subgroup contrast at unit-level i), lattice(all 3) zeroes the VCV on these 4-12-unit cells (no lattice config hosted), and poisson runs at i=st because a zero singleton treated cell is refused as separation (real_pois).

name: dta_s_strclus
rationale: Small clean panel (24 units x 10, 8 treated / 16 never, noise) whose only awkwardness is a string-typed cluster column strc with a value-identical numeric twin g — an everyday real-world coding, and an interface type refusal rather than a statistical degeneracy: the data itself admits a trustworthy answer via g. Sole config is an rc-parity refusal screen (109/109 on both builds, no results either way).

name: dta_s_ttbig
rationale: Identical shape to the well-behaved dta_s_ttyear but with time codes at extreme magnitude (t = 500000..500012, cohorts 500006/500009) — an unusual-but-holdable coding engineered to expose v1.3's silently inert timetrends. A correct implementation produces real trustworthy trend results (the HEAD pin), so the data admits a correct answer; it tests feature function at extreme codes.

name: dta_s_ttyear
rationale: Realistic calendar-year panel: 40 units x 2000-2012, cohorts 2006/2009 plus 16 never-treated, mild common trend plus small deterministic unit-trend heterogeneity so timetrends has real signal, and a ycount outcome for the poisson variant. Its A12 trigger is a ~1e-8-class numerical carve-out difference, i.e., feature-quality signal on sound data.

name: binary_balanced.dta
rationale: Fully balanced 12-cohort x 12-period panel (reps 3), staggered onsets 6/7/8 plus three never-treated cohorts, deterministic non-degenerate outcomes with pre/post periods everywhere. Workhorse for the 221-config ext grid; result differences here are feature-quality signal.

name: binary_fine.dta
rationale: Same balanced master data with cohort replaced by the unit id, i.e. the modal real-world unit-level panel: 36 units x 12 periods, 9 never-treated units, one obs per unit-period. Singleton cohort-period cells are nominal here (cohort := panel unit), not the degenerate-cell harm mechanism; trustworthy answers are fully available.

name: binary_mixed_grain.dta
rationale: Balanced rich panel (reps 8) whose panel identifier mixed_i_rich deliberately varies in grain across cohorts, with asserted cell sizes 1, 2, 3, and 8. Mixed grain is a canonical stress structure: awkward but plausibly realistic, results still usable, tests robustness and feature function together.

name: binary_mixed_imbalanced.dta
rationale: Reps-3 master with whole cohort-period cells dropped, used through the mixed-grain id mixed_i: imbalance plus mixed grain, and the dropped cells include the esrelativeto(-2) reference cells for cohorts 2 and 8. Controls and pre/post survive and wooldid runs rc 0/0; the upstream honestdid crash is exactly the observable robustness signal stress data exists to produce.

name: continuous_control_compact.dta
rationale: Full balanced master sample at reps 4: never-treated control cohorts, dense within-cell dose variation with engineered common support in every cohort-period cell, deterministic outcomes. Mainline data for the 45-config continuous ext grid.

name: continuous_control_dense.dta
rationale: Same design at reps 12: 1728 obs, never-treated controls, common-support dose, plus asserted exact 0.25/0.50 cell means making count-family oracle checks deterministic. Richest well-behaved continuous fixture; feeds the extlattice grid.

name: continuous_imbalanced_dense.dta
rationale: Reps-12 sample with selected cohort-period cells dropped, but engineered to stay estimable: the generator asserts every surviving cell keeps all 12 obs and every treated cohort keeps its t=ttre-2 reference cell. Deliberately awkward calendar gaps, deliberately not degenerate.

name: continuous_untreated_zero.dta
rationale: Content-identical to continuous_control_dense (same full reps-12 sample, same keep list; only the fixture-id char differs) - the untreated-zero identification scheme lives in which dose variable configs pick (dose_common_zero), not in any data degeneracy.

name: continuous_within_compact.dta
rationale: Reps-4 master with every never-treated cohort removed (keep if ttre < .) - a doctrine-listed degeneracy marker that is rescued only because its 36 grid configs all use contreatwithin, whose within-treated dose contrasts need no untreated controls. Estimand-conditional trustworthiness is the middle class; stress still credits its feature-function evidence.

name: survey_rcs.dta
rationale: Rich repeated-cross-section survey design: 24 states x 2 groups x 8 waves x 6 respondents, never-treated states 19-24, survey weights, and missingness that is weight-symmetric, treated-cells-only, with an asserted floor of 4 obs per cell. The SI-7 knife-edge fires in one of five configs and only under fe(i.group##i.t) - spec-induced, resolved with an observable caution, not a data degeneracy.

name: # unused-but-built fixtures (no config references them; comment rows so the stale check stays clean):
# continuous_within_dense.dta: stress per the 2026-08-29 wave (classified from generator code alone)

# continuous_untreated_zero_compact.dta: wellbehaved if a config is ever pointed at it - byte-identical to continuous_control_compact.dta (cf _all rc 0; datasets audit 2026-09-12); the 2026-08-29 wave said stress from generator code alone
# ---- inline-prep configs (dataset column empty; data built by the prep) ----
config:cont_sg_tidose
rationale: Rich 50x13 continuous panel, within-cohort dose variation, subgroups; the att side is trustworthy feature evidence. But dose is time-invariant per unit, so the sg-ame block is unidentified (SI-A4 d3 class, voided with caution - ledger SIA4-td-*): read ame-family cells as handle-it-correctly signal only. Coordinator adjudication 2026-08-29 (draft said wellbehaved but missed the SIA4-td rows).

name: config:trig_esfsup_ref
rationale: Prep esfsup_refdrop builds a tiny 14-unit panel and then deletes ALL never-treated observations at t=3, exactly the fixed base period of the onset-4 cohort — knife-edge estimability engineered so that cohort's reference cell has no control support and a trustworthy answer for it is impossible. This config runs it under safety(off), where old is silently wrong; the question is correct-or-observable handling.

name: config:trig_tm2_sgjoint
rationale: Prep tm2_sgjoint builds a grouped panel (15 cohort-ids x 6 subunits x 12 periods, N=1080) with dose variation, three never-treated groups, and deliberately planted sg-specific pre-trends — signal the sg joint pre-trend test SHOULD detect (probe p ~1e-13/1e-36; att twins pin bit-identical). Uniform subunit replication per i x t is ordinary grouped data, not degeneracy; result differences here are feature-quality signal.

name: config:trig_d3void
rationale: Prep d3void makes dose a pure function of the id i (time- and subunit-invariant within i), so the requested contreat/ame dose-slope estimand is unidentified by construction — every treated-cell slope drops collinear, and old fabricates plausible-looking ame zeros, the exact failure class pathological data exists to probe. The att rows stay clean and bit-identical, but the void probe is the dominant purpose.

name: config:trig_esfsup_ref322
rationale: Same engineered data as trig_esfsup_ref (prep esfsup_refdrop): the never-treated pool is deleted at exactly the onset-4 cohort's fixed base period, making that cohort's reference unsupported by construction. This companion config runs default safety and pins the rc pair only — old aborts opaquely r322, new drops the refless cohort gracefully: purely a correct-or-observable-failure probe.

name: # ---- per-config overrides: the prep/ifcond changes the effective data class ----
config:ext_contract10_fractional_time
rationale: prep 'recast double t; replace t = 1.5 if t == 1' breaks the integer time grid of binary_balanced.dta (configs_ext.csv row 346, rc 0->459 under safety(on)): fractional time coding, validation-screen probe.

name: config:ext_contract10_if_outside_negative
rationale: prep 'replace y_count_oracle = -1 if cohort == 12' plants a negative-outcome sentinel ONLY OUTSIDE the ifcond window (ifcond 'cohort < 12'; configs_ext.csv row 353, rc 411->322): the in-sample data is clean — the case probes whether input screening respects if-scope, and both builds abort. Labeling this run wellbehaved would mislead triage into reading the rc divergence as a feature defect on good data.

name: config:ext_contract10_inconsistent_ttre
rationale: prep 'replace ttre = 7 if cohort == 1 & mod(wdbt_obs_id, 2) == 0' makes onset vary WITHIN cohort 1's units over time (configs_ext.csv row 347, rc 0->459): within-unit inconsistent onset — invalid design, same B-F13 class as dta_s_mintsent's ttre column.

name: config:ext_contract10_nonpositive_time
rationale: prep 'replace t = 0 if t == 1' plants a nonpositive period and a spacing gap in the time grid (configs_ext.csv row 345, safety(on)): engineered invalid clock; the case exists to pin the safety screen, not to yield results.

name: config:ext_contract_fractional_lattice
rationale: prep 'replace custom_lattice = 1.5 if custom_lattice == 1' (configs_ext.csv row 314, rc 452/452 'factor variables may not contain noninteger values'): non-integer lattice factor — sentinel coding, observable-refusal pin.

name: config:ext_contract_fractional_subgroup
rationale: prep 'replace sg_three = 1.5 if cohort == 1' on binary_balanced.dta (configs_ext.csv row 312, rc 198->411 '_joint_horiz_i_s1.5 invalid name'): non-integer subgroup sentinel coding.

name: config:ext_contract_split_subgroup
rationale: prep 'replace sg_three = 2 if cohort == 1 & mod(wdbt_obs_id, 2) == 0' splits cohort 1's observations across subgroups within units (wdbt_obs_id varies over t), run under safety(off) (configs_ext.csv row 313): straddler coding, same invalid-design class as scr_sgsplit_off.

name: config:ext_cov10_cont_within_vary
rationale: prep ext_cov10_cont_within_vary ('keep if ttre < .') drops all never-treated cohorts from continuous_control_dense.dta (wellbehaved), but the config carries contreatwithin (configs_ext.csv row 330) — the same estimand-conditional rescue that puts continuous_within_compact/dense in stress; keep it consistent with those siblings.

name: config:ext_path10_cont_constant_dose
rationale: prep generates dose_constant = 1 and the config runs contreat(dose_constant) (configs_ext.csv row 341): zero dose variation makes every treated-cell dose slope collinear-dropped — the identical unidentified-estimand construction as trig_d3void, which the draft itself classes pathological.

name: config:ext_path10_no_never_treated
rationale: prep ext_path10_no_never_treated (preps.json: 'keep if ttre < .') deletes cohorts 10-12, the ONLY never-treated pool in binary_balanced.dta, and the config runs the resulting no-never binary design under safety(off) (configs_ext.csv row 343). No-never-treated is the doctrine's explicit pathological marker; unlike the within_* fixtures there is no contreatwithin rescue.

name: config:ext_path10_ppml_separation
rationale: prep zeroes y_count_oracle for an entire cohort-period cell ('replace y_count_oracle = 0 if cohort == 1 & t == 6') on continuous_control_dense.dta — engineered Poisson perfect separation (msg pin 'conformability error', configs_ext.csv row 338), the scheme's explicit pathological marker; same class as dta_path_sep.

name: config:ext_path10_sparse_subgroup
rationale: prep 'drop if sg_three == 1 & t < 5' on binary_balanced.dta leaves sg1's earliest cohort (cohort 1, ttre 6) a single pre period (t=5) while esprelength(2)+timetrends are requested (configs_ext.csv row 342): deliberately sparse subgroup pre-support, but every cohort keeps its reference cell and the run completes rc 0/0 — relyrgap-class gap stress, not degeneracy.

name: config:ext_san_input_missing
rationale: prep plants exactly one missing/zero in each of 9 input columns (y, cohort, t, x1, person_id, analytic_weight x2, dose, custom_lattice) on rows that ENTER the sample; the pin is the sanitizer's '9 obs dropped from initial sample' message with rc 0/0 (configs_ext.csv row 306). A trustworthy answer exists (drop the 9 rows) — missing-input robustness on sound data, the same logic that puts dta_s_extmiss in stress. Distinct from scr_badif, whose bad rows are if-excluded and whose surviving run is clean (no override there).

name: config:ext_val10_fractional_ttre
rationale: prep 'recast double ttre; replace ttre = 6.5 if cohort == 1' plants a fractional in-window onset (configs_ext.csv row 355, rc 452->459): absurd coding whose only correct outcome is an observable refusal.

name: config:ext_val10_mismatched_clock
rationale: prep sets ttre = 2006 for all treated units against the t = 1..12 clock (configs_ext.csv row 359, rc 459/459 'cannot find either a treated time period'): no treated period exists in-window — degenerate by construction.

name: config:ext_val10_zero_coded_never
rationale: prep 'replace ttre = 0 if missing(ttre)' recodes the never-treated pool to sentinel 0 (configs_ext.csv row 356, rc 459/459 'no never-treated control group'): sentinel coding is on the scheme's explicit pathological list; the only question is the observable refusal.

name: config:ext_val_negative_weight
rationale: prep 'replace analytic_weight = -1 in 1' (configs_ext.csv row 305, rc 411/411 'weights must not be negative'): invalid input, refusal pin.

name: config:ext_val_nonpositive_id
rationale: prep 'replace cohort = 0 if cohort == 1' plants nonpositive unit ids (configs_ext.csv row 302, rc 411/411 'must consist of positive, non-zero integers'): sentinel id coding, refusal pin.

name: config:ext_val_poisson_negative_y
rationale: prep 'replace y_count = -1 in 1' plants a negative count outcome for a poisson run (configs_ext.csv row 303, rc 411/411): invalid input, observable-failure question only.

name: config:scr_fracttre
rationale: prep fract_ttre ('replace ttre = ttre + 0.5 if ttre < .') makes ALL onsets in dta_binary fractional (configs.csv row 94, rc 0->459, note 'old mislabeled silently'): same fractional-onset sentinel class as ext_val10_fractional_ttre, on a dataset classed wellbehaved.

name: config:scr_nonintsg
rationale: prep sgf_nonint ('gen sgf = cond(ttre < ., 1.5, 1)') creates a non-integer subgroup on dta_binary (configs.csv row 87, rc 198->411): invalid coding, refusal-quality pin only.

name: config:scr_sgsplit
rationale: prep sgstr_straddle makes sgstr switch from 1 to 2 at t>2006 WITHIN treated units on dta_binary (configs.csv row 95, rc 0->459): subgroup straddling a unit is an invalid design (subgroups must be cohort-level); pure refusal probe.

name: config:scr_sgsplit_off
rationale: same sgstr_straddle prep run under safety(off) (configs.csv row 96, note 'att/att_it expected EQUAL'): the coding stays invalid-by-design; the run answers only the correct-or-observable-behavior question, not feature quality.

name: config:sg_degpre
rationale: prep sgd2_degpre (preps.json) reassigns ttre to the second sample year (2001) for the 11 units with mod(i,7)==0 and makes them subgroup sgd2==2 on dta_binary (configs.csv row 23): that subgroup is a cohort with exactly one pre period, so the esprelength(2) pre window is partially nonexistent for it — an engineered degenerate-pre subgroup probe, but the reference period exists and the overall run stays estimable.

name: config:fcol_sg
rationale: prep adm_sub + i=cohid with subgroups(region) under safety(off): region varies within every cohid unit (4 of 4; inventory 2026-09-12), so the subgroup straddles the cohort id - the same invalid-design class as scr_sgsplit_off; the run answers only the handle-it-correctly question for fastcollapse x straddling subgroups, not feature quality.

name: config:cont_sg_gap
rationale: prep dose2_sgr: dose2 = f(i) only (0/280 i x t cells and 0/30 units vary; inventory 2026-09-12), so the sg-ame block is unidentified (SI-A4 d3 class) on top of relyrgap's gaps - read ame-family cells as handle-it-correctly signal only, as for cont_sg_tidose.

name: config:real_sg
rationale: P1 (wellbehaved) run with i=unit nested in cluster(st) and subgroups(sg): the pairwise subgroup-contrast covariance is rank-deficient in the contrast direction (SI-A1 sg-contrast class; the run prints the '2 pairwise row(s)' caution and blanks those rows - critique of D-4, crit2 2026-09-13), and an i=st twin is refused because sg varies within st (r459). The per-subgroup atts are trustworthy; the contrast rows are a handle-it-correctly pin, not subgroup-quality evidence.
